tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). 4	 * "Data source"; docs.cfo.ai/integrations/connect-and-sync-data, /workspace-settings/file-attachments-in-chat).
5	 * cfo.ai's Ari then models COGS per monitored contract from these rows instead of from typed
6	 * guesses. One row per real bundle (live and replay, labeled); values are the bundle's own.
7	 * No real bundles → the header only (never placeholder rows).
8	 *
9	 * packages/web/src/pages/business/model.ts renders the same CSV in the browser for the download
10	 * button; packages/web/test/business-page.test.ts checks the two stay byte-identical.
11	 */
12	import type { EconomicsFile } from "../schema/economics.js";

34	const field = (v: string | number | null): string => {
35	  if (v === null) return "";
36	  const s = String(v);
37	  return /[",\r\n]/.test(s) ? `"${s.replaceAll('"', '""')}"` : s;
38	};

40	export function renderCfoInputsCsv(file: Pick<EconomicsFile, "computed">): string {
41	  const rows = (file.computed?.runs ?? []).map((r) =>
42	    [

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

content.content:
**Server and transport**
- URL: `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`
- Transport: HTTP (remote MCP server). Claude Code setup uses `--transport http`.

**Authentication**
- Browser-based sign-in with a cfo.ai account. In Claude Code, you select the server in `/mcp` and choose Authenticate. In Codex, you run `codex mcp login cfoai`.
- You must be logged into the correct cfo.ai account and have access to the target workspace.
- The page does not specify OAuth client registration, redirect URIs, or scopes.

**Supported clients**
- Claude Code
- Codex
- Other harnesses that support remote MCP servers, added as a custom connector or MCP server

**Tools**

| Tool | Type (per name) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `list_orgs` | Read | Lists workspaces for multi-workspace accounts |
| `inspect_table_blocks` | Read | Example: `{"read": {"target": "Operating Plan"}}` |
| `edit_table_blocks` | Write | |
| `inspect_pages` | Read | |
| `edit_pages` | Write | |
| `inspect_canvas_library` | Read | |
| `edit_canvas_blocks` | Write | |
| `inspect_scenarios` | Read | |
| `edit_scenarios` | Write | |
| `edit_dimension_mappings` | Write | |
| `inspect_integrations` | Read | |
| `edit_integrations` | Write | |
| `inspect_skills` | Read | |
| `edit_triggers` | Write | |
| `inspect_documentation` | Read | |

The page gives no descriptions or full input schemas for these tools. The only parameter details are:
- Multi-action tools take exactly one block named for the action.
- For multi-workspace accounts, `org_id` (a workspace ID or slug from `list_orgs`) is passed on each later tool call.

Tools designed for in-app use, such as asking a question in chat or playing a Guide, are not published.

**Writes**
- Writes apply to the selected live workspace. To work on an alternative plan without changing Main, use a Scenario.

**Rate limits**
- None are stated.

**Tools named on the page**

- `inspect_skills`: `list` block (find the `build-model` skill) and `instructions` block (read it)
- `inspect_pages`, `inspect_scenarios`, `inspect_dimension_mappings`: read existing Model content. No argument shapes given.
- `inspect_table_blocks`: read saved tables
- `edit_table_blocks`: create, update, and delete saved tables, Variables, Dimensions, and formulas
- `edit_pages`: Page and block changes
- `edit_dimension_mappings`, `edit_scenarios`: change Dimension mappings and Scenarios
- `inspect_canvas_library`: search and read Canvas components
- `edit_canvas_blocks`: create and update Canvas blocks
- `validate_code_blocks`: renders saved Canvas blocks in a browser
- `inspect_history`: `changelog` view
- `list_orgs`: lists workspaces

**Argument shapes**

- `inspect_table_blocks`:
  ```json
  { "read": { "target": "Operating Plan" } }
  ```
- `edit_table_blocks` update (one block named for the action; `scenario` may sit beside it):
  ```json
  {
    "update": {
      "target": "Operating Plan",
      "row_updates": [
        {
          "rows": ["Gross Margin"],
          "default_formulas": { "forecast": { "formula": "iferror(`Gross Profit` / Revenue, 0)" } }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
  ```
  - Rows on dated tables take `default_formulas` with `actuals`, `forecast`, or both.
  - Rows on timeless tables take `formula`.
- `edit_table_blocks` create: takes a `tables` list, so several dependent tables can go in one call. Field names inside each table are not given.
- `edit_table_blocks` delete: can list `variables` or `dimensions`. Deletion is refused when other objects read them unless `force: true` is set.
- `inspect_pages`, `inspect_scenarios`: no argument shapes given.
- `list_orgs`: no argument shape given. Pass the chosen workspace's ID or slug as `org_id` on later calls.
- `edit_canvas_blocks` create: requires `page`, `title`, and `source`.
- `edit_canvas_blocks` update: `source_patches` (a list of exact `old` to `new` replacements, each matching once) or `source` (replaces the whole component).
- `inspect_canvas_library` list: takes a `query` of search words. `read` takes up to 16 targets.
- `inspect_history` changelog: takes `search`.

**Response shapes**

- `inspect_history` reports `entries_searched`.
- Canvas writes without a browser render return a `render_unverified` warning. With `validate: true`, the browser result appears under `validation`.
- Validation results include an `observed` sentence and, for colors, `source_notes`.
- Failed renders return `browser_validation_unavailable` with `transient: true`.
- Write receipts show references like `Name#hex`, which you reuse in later calls.
- Dataset rows hold each Variable's value: a number, text, an ISO date, `"true"`/`"false"`, or `null`.

**Table block structure**

- Tables are either dated (with actuals and forecast formulas per row) or timeless (one formula per row).
- Rows belong to tables and reference Variables and Dimensions by name.
- The page does not describe columns, periods, or value fields in detail.

**Creating a new table**

Use `edit_table_blocks` with a `create` block containing a `tables` list. The page points to a separate reference (`/formulas/agent-docs/create-and-update`) for the full shapes, which were not included here. Before writing, read `build-model` with `inspect_skills`, and use `inspect_pages` and `inspect_table_blocks` to check existing content.

content.content:
The page documents only one exact JSON argument shape, for reading a saved Table Block:

```json
{
  "scenario": "Main",
  "read": {
    "target": "Revenue by Customer",
    "formula_origins": "all"
  }
}
```

It does not include argument shapes for `values`, `evaluate`, or `periods`, and it does not show the response shape or any response JSON examples.

The page also names these fields without giving their JSON shapes:

- **`rows` and `columns`**: row and column references copied from a prior response, used to narrow a follow-up read.
- **`depth`**: includes the members beneath a selected row.
- **`as_of_point`**: used for historical reads against the same table and target.
- **`compare`** with **`before_change_log_id`**: shows how a table changed since a saved change.
- **`dry_run: true`**: on an `edit_table_blocks` write, validates the change without saving it. The page says the result returns `valid`, `warnings`, and `model_effects`.

The document covers only part of this. It gives no `list`, `values`, or period-range actions for `inspect_table_blocks`, and it does not define a full response schema. Below is what it does state.

## Request shapes

**Saved formulas for one Variable** (verbatim):
```json
{
  "scenario": "Main",
  "variable": { "target": "Gross Margin" }
}
```

**Several Variables or Dimensions in one call** (verbatim; one entry per reference, in the order given):
```json
{
  "scenario": "Main",
  "variable": { "target": ["Amount#a4d", "Probability#058"] }
}
```

**Visible table values with formula origins** (verbatim):
```json
{
  "scenario": "Main",
  "read": {
    "target": "Operating Plan",
    "rows": ["Gross Margin"],
    "formula_origins": "all"
  }
}
```

**Table read at a coarser grain** (verbatim):
```json
{
  "scenario": "Main",
  "read": { "target": "Operating Plan", "rows": ["Bookings"], "grain": "YEAR" }
}
```

**Other documented options (no verbatim example):**
- `variable` block: `conditions` (one exact saved scope) and `after` (paging cursor, copied from `next.after`, with the same `target`).
- `dimension` block: same pattern as `variable`; `items` lists members.
- `read` block: `columns` (period references, one per Scenario and period when comparing), `comparison` (`"none"` required for `include_inputs` and `recalculate`), `formula_origins` (`"all"` or `"zeros"`), `grain` (`"QUARTER"` or `"YEAR"`), `include_inputs` (`true`, with one row and one column selected), `recalculate` (`true`).
- `as_of_point`: historical reads. `bounds` refuses it.

## Response fields named in the document

- **Saved-formula read:** one entry per formula definition, with its condition and Actuals or Forecast range. Each entry has `scope` (with `time_grain` and reach), `source_default` (with `order`, for imported sources), and `dependents` (`total`, `formulas`, `blocks`, `settings`, `manual_items`, `inaccessible`, `items`). Paged results include `next` with `after`.
- **Table read:**
  - `rows` and `columns`. Column entries include `ref`, `axis`, `dimension`, `grain`, and `writable`, e.g. `{"ref": "Date#10b", "axis": true, "dimension": "Date", "grain": "MONTH", "writable": true}`.
  - Row references such as `Revenue[West][Enterprise]` and `Amount#a4d`, with `#` plus a hex suffix.
  - Rows carry `member` and `members`, and a rule that may include `formula`, `clear_formula`, and `readOnlyReason` (or `read_only_reason` with `writable: false` on rows and columns).
  - `inherited_from` names the owner and condition of an outside rule.
  - `calculation.source`: one of `cached`, `promoted`, `derived`, `seeded`, `full`, `recalculated`.
  - `issues`, with `category` (`capacity`, `model`, `request`, `dependency`, `internal`) and `transient`.
  - `coverage`, which can read `incomplete`.
  - `sources`, keyed by `query_ref`.
- **Cell values:** the document says a cell that breaks its row's rule "says so in the cell," and that grain-rollup gaps show `#NO_ROLLUP`. It does not name the key that holds cell values.
- **Scenario:** the document names the requested Scenario but does not describe a `scenario` key in the response.

## cfo.ai MCP integration and the economics audit fixes: what changed

Nothing is committed. PLAN.md and DECISIONS.md are untouched. Proposed DECISIONS entries are at the end.

### Results
- **Core:** typecheck is clean and all 1022 tests pass, including the new `test/cfo.test.ts` (22 tests).
- **Web:** typecheck has 1 error and 4 tests fail. All of them are in other agents' in-progress work, not in files I touched:
  - the typecheck error is in `src/pages/incidents/IncidentsPage.tsx` (line 263: `entry` does not exist).
  - 3 failures are in `test/incidents-page.test.ts`.
  - 1 failure is in `test/real-runs.test.ts` (fixture count: expected 9, got 8).
  - Before their edits landed the web suite was fully green (295/295).
  - My `test/cfo-panel.test.ts`, `business-page`, `docs-page` and `data-boundary` all pass.
- **`pnpm check:secrets`:** clean.
- **`pnpm notary cfo status` (real):** "not connected: No cfo.ai sign-in stored", plus the connect command.
- **`pnpm notary cfo connect --discover-only` (real, via the MCP SDK):**
  - protected resource: `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`
  - authorization server and authorization endpoint host: `complete-cottage-73.authkit.app` (WorkOS AuthKit)
  - dynamic client registration, PKCE S256, public clients and refresh tokens: all yes
  - It stopped before registering a client or opening the browser.
  - So a command-line client with a loopback redirect is supported, and the Claude Code fallback isn't needed.
- **Business page:** I checked it in the preview browser in replay mode. The panel renders with "Not synced from cfo.ai yet" and both commands. Live mode is covered by tests only; I didn't run it against a live `notary serve`.

### What works
- **`notary cfo connect [--org <id>] [--discover-only]`**
  - Uses the SDK's OAuth: discovery, dynamic client registration, authorization code with PKCE.
  - Listens on `http://127.0.0.1:<random port>/callback` and checks the `state` value.
  - Opens your default browser; on Windows it uses `rundll32`, with no shell involved.
  - Each connect starts a fresh sign-in.
  - Tokens are saved to `packages/core/config/cfo-oauth.json`: gitignored, mode 0600, written atomically, never printed.
